Every entry below is a NAMED, documented exception -- never a bulk allowlist. A closing commit that fixes a violation MUST shrink the matching list in the SAME commit (relocation atomicity: the fix and the baseline shrink together).

production_family1_cross_package_private._note: HARD-ZERO (2026-07): the application.review <-> application.workflow cycle-break documented here has been structurally removed. WorkflowEvent, utc_now, InvoiceReviewRecord, and LedgerReviewRecord -- the four runtime-bound names each side needed from the other -- were extracted into a new shared leaf module, cadrumo.application._workflow_review_models, that neither application.review nor application.workflow depends on; both packages now import these names from that shared owner instead of from each other's private submodules. Every consumer outside these two packages is unaffected: they already imported through the public application.review / application.workflow facades, which keep re-exporting the same names from the new owner. The gate now asserts the production count is EXACTLY ZERO (see the corresponding hard-zero assertion in test_import_hygiene_gate.py) rather than ratcheting against a named baseline; sites stays [] and any new production Family-1 hit is a straight failure.

family2_shim_modules._note: Every module the scanner classifies as a Family-2 shim / pure-reexport surface. Now EMPTY: the last documented bridge, src/cadrumo/domain/transactions/_ids.py, is gone -- its consumers resolve TransactionId through cadrumo.core.identity, the canonical owner. The operator directive is that a symbol has exactly one home and is imported from it, so a re-export module is no longer an acceptable canonical source at all. The gate fails if ANY shim appears; do not re-add a path here to make a new bridge pass.

family2_delegate_wrapper_shims._note: The same no-standing-bridge rule as family2_shim_modules, in the syntax that evades a def-counting check: a public callable whose whole body re-calls another package's symbol with its own arguments unchanged. EMPTY by intent, and the gate fails if ANY appears. An entry here is a NAMED exception with a stated reason, keyed by (path, function) so it survives every edit that only moves the code -- it is not a mute button, and a stale entry (one whose callable is no longer a forwarding wrapper) fails the gate just as loudly as an undocumented one. Before adding an entry, prefer the fix: point the consumers at the canonical owner and delete the wrapper.

family3_pinned_duplicate_symbols._note: Named Family-3 'genuine duplicate' symbols with an investigated, pinned disposition.
